title: Part VII
author: David Hume
summary: Philo argues that the world resembles a plant or an animal more than a work of art, so it might have arisen by vegetation or generation rather than design. If the Brahmins say the world was spun by a great spider, he asks, what has Cleanthes to oppose them with but his own preference?

notes.note: A transcription error for *seed*: the 1779 printing has *ſeed*, with a long s.

notes.on: Hesiod, and all the ancient Mythologists
notes.note: Hesiod's *Theogony* tells the origin of the world and the gods as a series of births.
The image of creation as a spider sending out its thread and drawing it back occurs in the Upanishads (*Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad*, i. 1. 7).
